stocks:TEL.OL.recent: Plaintiffs in Oslo sued Telenor, saying it gave Myanmar's junta 1,253 phone numbers and then sold the network, with its call records and location data, to a junta-linked buyer. The suit was filed after the last close on the chart, so it does not explain the slide before it.

wiki-china.standing: The daily count of readers of Wikipedia's article on China, the world's second-largest economy and its largest exporter. It shows how often the country's affairs send a general audience to look it up.
wiki-china.recent: Beijing's fortnight ran from an EU plan to cut imports of Chinese hybrid cars by half, which state media answered with a warning against 'new tricks', to a draft list of 23 AI technologies it would curb for export, and a central bank that bought 23 tonnes of gold in September. None of it falls on the day of the high.

stocks:FFH.TO.standing: A Toronto holding company that owns property and casualty insurers and reinsurers around the world and invests their premiums, run by Prem Watsa in a value style. It has built large stakes in Indian companies.
stocks:FFH.TO.recent: Fairfax won 60.72% of IDBI Bank for ₹52,878 crore, India's largest privatisation, which puts the insurer's balance sheet in control of an Indian lender. The award came after the chart's last close, so none of the line reflects it, and nothing in the input explains the earlier moves.

stocks:PLTR.standing: Palantir Technologies, a US software company listed on Nasdaq, sells data-analysis platforms to defence ministries, intelligence agencies and large corporations. Government contracts make up a large share of its revenue.
stocks:PLTR.recent: France chose Chapsvision over another Palantir contract as European governments questioned their dependence on the company, and Louis Mosley warned that Europe was 'missing the boat' on AI. Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the share price itself.

stocks:GFS.standing: A contract chipmaker that builds other companies' designs, specialising in older, cheaper process nodes used in cars, phones, radios and defence electronics. It is one of the few foundries headquartered in the US.
stocks:GFS.recent: Washington doubled its equity stake in GlobalFoundries to nearly 8% and will partner with it on a new fab at Malta, New York, a step from CHIPS Act grants to outright ownership. The deal came after this chart's last close, so it does not account for the rise shown here.

stocks:RELIANCE.NS.standing: India's most valuable listed company, a Mumbai conglomerate that runs the Jamnagar refining complex alongside Jio telecoms and India's biggest retail chain. Its size makes it a swing stock for the whole Indian market.
stocks:RELIANCE.NS.recent: Reliance is floating Jio Platforms, its telecom arm, in what it priced as India's largest offering, seeking up to ₹30,213 crore; the $3.2 billion sale drew nearly Rs 2.5 lakh crore of demand, sovereign funds among the bidders. Separately, Reliance answered Musk over Starlink, saying its own satellite service awaits the same clearances.

stocks:ACN.standing: One of the world's largest consulting and IT-services firms, incorporated in Ireland and listed in New York. Its shares track how much corporations spend on outsourcing, and lately on help adopting AI.
stocks:ACN.recent: The one story about Accenture's own business was a cost cut: staff who had spent up to $1,000 a month on Claude were capped at $29, a firm that sells AI transformation to clients now rationing it for its own workers. It landed at the end of the rise, which began in late September, and does not account for it.

stocks:NESN.SW.standing: The world's largest packaged-food company, based in Vevey, Switzerland, selling Nescafé, Maggi, Purina and infant formula almost everywhere. A heavyweight of the Swiss SMI, its share moves with coffee, cocoa and dairy costs.

stocks:BA.L.standing: Britain's largest defence company, building warships, nuclear submarines, combat aircraft and munitions, with a large US arm. Its shares move on NATO governments' defence budgets and the export orders they approve.
stocks:BA.L.recent: A cyberattack on BAE Systems, working as a contractor for the US courts, halted all notices for US bankruptcy courts. The attack was reported in Washington after the slide had already happened, and nothing else in the input explains the price.

stocks:TSLA.standing: Shares in Tesla, the US maker of electric cars and grid batteries, listed on Nasdaq. Its valuation rests more on bets about self-driving cars and robots than on the cars it sells today, so it moves on Elon Musk's promises.
stocks:TSLA.recent: The fortnight's news about Tesla's own business was Musk's push into India stalling alongside Starlink, and the debut of a 2026 Roadster priced at at least $200,000, which came after the latest reading on the chart. Neither accounts for the share's path across the window.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Apple's shares, traded on the Nasdaq. Most of its revenue comes from the iPhone, and its weight as one of the world's most valuable companies means its moves carry the S&P 500 and Nasdaq indices with it.
stocks:AAPL.recent: Pre-orders for the iPhone Duo opened and the phone was backordered until 2027 on the first day. In the same week Apple Intelligence entered China running on Alibaba's Qwen models, the route Apple took to approval there. Days earlier Apple introduced HomeView, a $299 tablet for the home.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: The first cryptocurrency, a fixed-supply digital currency run on a public ledger with no central issuer, launched in 2009. Its price sets the tone for the whole crypto market, and funds, banks and listed companies now hold it.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: Nothing reported from early October accounts for the spike. The fortnight since turned on quantum risk: 6.4 million bitcoin sit behind exposed public keys, Google says Willow cut magic-state errors about 40-fold, and Coinbase urged a quantum-resistant migration. MSCI's rules put treasury firms Strategy and Metaplanet on notice.

stocks:MSTR.standing: A Nasdaq-listed software company that became the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, funding its purchases by selling new shares and debt. Its stock trades as a leveraged bet on the bitcoin price.
stocks:MSTR.recent: MSCI finalised rules that can eject companies whose main business is holding bitcoin from its equity indexes, putting Strategy and Japan's Metaplanet on notice. JPMorgan estimates $2.8 billion of forced selling of Strategy shares. The funds sell the stock, not the bitcoin, which squeezes the cheap equity the firm raises to buy more.

stocks:JPM.standing: America's largest bank by assets, spanning Chase consumer branches, a leading investment bank and a vast trading operation. Its quarterly results open US bank earnings season and are read as a check on the economy's health.
stocks:JPM.recent: Fed officials questioned JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley in a review of bank lending to private credit, prompted by worries over that market. When results arrived, a $1.2B money laundering penalty drove Bank of America to an earnings miss while JPMorgan Chase held steady.

stocks:3350.T.standing: A Tokyo-listed company that turned from running budget hotels to holding bitcoin as its main asset, and sells new shares to buy more. Its stock works as a leveraged bet on bitcoin for investors in Japan.
stocks:3350.T.recent: MSCI finalised rules that can eject companies whose main business is holding bitcoin from its equity indexes, Metaplanet among them. Index funds then sell the shares, not the bitcoin, which cuts at the cheap equity the firm raises to buy more; JPMorgan put the forced selling of Strategy alone at $2.8 billion.

stocks:MSCI.standing: The New York company whose stock indexes, among them MSCI World and MSCI Emerging Markets, decide what trillions of dollars in tracking funds must own. It also sells ESG ratings and risk analytics, and its fees grow with the assets benchmarked to it.
stocks:MSCI.recent: MSCI finalised rules that can eject bitcoin-holding firms such as Strategy and Metaplanet from its indexes, with JPMorgan estimating $2.8 billion of forced selling of Strategy alone. It also moved to strip Indonesia of emerging-market status, sending Jakarta to a six-year low. Nothing reported ties either decision to MSCI's own share price.

stocks:HSBA.L.standing: One of Europe's largest banks, headquartered in London but earning most of its profit in Asia, above all in Hong Kong. Its London shares move on Asian interest rates and on the state of relations between China and the West.

stocks:TSM.standing: Shares of the world's largest contract chipmaker, which fabricates the most advanced processors for Apple, Nvidia and others from plants in Taiwan. Its order book is a direct read on demand for AI and smartphone chips.

stocks:INTC.standing: An American chipmaker that both designs and manufactures its own processors, which run most PCs and many servers. Its foundry arm, making chips for other firms, carries Washington's push for US-made semiconductors.

stocks:JD.standing: One of China's largest online retailers, listed in New York and Hong Kong. Unlike its rivals it owns its warehouses and delivery fleet, so its sales track what Chinese households are spending.
stocks:JD.recent: The fortnight carried one story about the company's own business: it ended deposit pre-sales for its 18th Singles' Day. That story ran after the shares had already peaked, and nothing in it accounts for the price.

wiki-international-monetary-fund.standing: The Washington-based lender to governments in balance-of-payments crises, owned by nearly every country. Its loans come with budget conditions, and its twice-yearly growth forecasts set the baseline finance ministries argue against.
wiki-international-monetary-fund.recent: The IMF and World Bank met in Bangkok under an energy shock: the Fund lifted its world growth forecast to 3.1% but cut the Gulf's, seeing Kuwait shrink 16.7% as the Hormuz closure dragged on. The IMF chief then warned that low-income countries spend up to 14% of revenue on debt and called for urgent fiscal repairs.

wiki-india.standing: Wikipedia's article on India, the world's most populous country and its largest democracy. How many people open it each day is a rough measure of how often the wider world stops to look the country up.
wiki-india.recent: Thousands marched in New Delhi demanding the election chief resign over a voter-roll revision that, media reports say, has removed 133 million names since last year. Police detained the 'cockroach' movement's leaders at Jantar Mantar, deployed 6,000 officers against its flag march, and turned Abhijeet Dipke's detention into an arrest.

poly-will-david-lisnard-win-the-2027-fre.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if David Lisnard, the centre-right mayor of Cannes, wins France's 2027 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

stocks:V.standing: The largest card payment network in the world, routing transactions between the banks that issue cards and those that accept them. It earns a fee on each payment and lends nothing, so its revenue tracks consumer spending.

stocks:CRCL.standing: The US company that issues USDC, a dollar stablecoin backed by cash and short-dated Treasuries. Most of its revenue is interest on those reserves, so the share tracks US short-term rates and how much USDC circulates.

poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist heading UN Trade and Development, becomes the next UN Secretary-General. The Security Council's five veto holders must all accept the nominee.

poly-ilhan-omar-federally-charged-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if federal prosecutors charge Ilhan Omar, the Democratic congresswoman from Minnesota, before its deadline. The price is what traders pay for that payout.

poly-edi-rama-out-as-albania-pm-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Edi Rama stops being Albania's prime minister before the end of 2026. Rama, leader of the Socialist Party, took office in 2013.

poly-yemeni-forces-enter-sanaa-by-novemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Yemen's government and allied forces enter Sanaa, the capital the Houthis have held since 2014, by November 30. Its price is what traders will pay on the city changing hands.
poly-yemeni-forces-enter-sanaa-by-novemb.recent: The government's offensive pushed along the coast, not toward Sanaa: it said it took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road on the way to Bab al-Mandeb. The Houthis meanwhile carried the war onto Saudi soil, striking Riyadh's airport until Lufthansa and Air India stopped flying there, and firing missiles at Yanbu.

stocks:LYFT.standing: Shares in Lyft, the second-largest ride-hailing app in the United States after Uber, sold almost entirely on the US and Canadian market. Its price turns on rider demand, driver pay and rules for gig workers.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-us-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Kamala Harris, the former vice-president and 2024 Democratic nominee, wins the 2028 US presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in cents on the dollar.

stocks:UBER.standing: Shares in Uber, the largest ride-hailing and food-delivery platform outside China, listed in New York. The price tracks how many trips and orders it brokers and how much of each fare it keeps.
stocks:UBER.recent: The one story about Uber's own business came after the last close shown. Consumer Reports looked into how its AI pricing sets fares and found that same-minute quotes for one trip differed by 42.4%. Nothing earlier in the input accounts for the share price.

poly-iran-oman-hormuz-agreement-by-octob.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Iran and Oman, the two states whose coasts form the Strait of Hormuz, reach an agreement on the strait before its deadline. About a fifth of the world's seaborne oil passes through that channel.
poly-iran-oman-hormuz-agreement-by-octob.recent: The only Hormuz deal on offer runs through Washington rather than Oman: in Baghdad, Araghchi offered to reopen the strait on a fixed timetable, with talks with the US to follow if it accepts Iran's conditions. Hours later the IRGC said another tanker had struck a mine, after a week in which 12 ships were attacked near Hormuz, a record.

wiki-volodymyr-zelenskyy.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the former actor and comedian elected Ukraine's president in 2019, who has led the country through Russia's full-scale invasion.
wiki-volodymyr-zelenskyy.recent: Trump said Zelenskyy had lost 30% of Ukraine and that Ukraine should elect a new president. Zelenskyy offered to stop refinery strikes if Russia halted energy attacks, then said Russia broke Trump's truce by striking a Kharkiv power plant. Within days, Ukraine had run out of Patriot interceptors.

poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Yemen's Houthi movement and Saudi Arabia agree a ceasefire by the end of October. Its price is what traders will stake on a truce, and Gulf oil exports and Red Sea shipping ride on it.
poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.recent: The war widened instead of pausing: a strike on Riyadh's airport killed 13, a missile set fire to an Aramco building in Dhahran, and the coalition struck Sanaa. Egypt's defence council approved troops for Saudi Arabia, though parliament delayed the vote, and the Houthis told Aramco shareholders to sell.

poly-will-google-have-the-best-ai-model-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Google holds the top-ranked AI model when October 2026 ends. It is a running bet on the race among the big labs, where a single model release can reorder the leaderboard overnight.

stocks:IBM.standing: The century-old American computing company, which earns most of its money from software such as Red Hat and from consulting for large enterprises and governments, and still builds the mainframes many banks run on.

poly-will-the-iranian-regime-fall-by-the.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Iran's Islamic Republic loses power before 2027. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome: a running bet on whether the clerical state outlasts war, sanctions and unrest.
poly-will-the-iranian-regime-fall-by-the.recent: Through the war with the US, Tehran's institutions kept working: parliament approved Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi, a sanctioned missile builder, as defence minister, and Araghchi, in Baghdad, offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within six days if Washington accepts Iran's terms. Pezeshkian claimed Iran no longer needs gasoline imports, per state agency Mehr.

poly-will-ron-desantis-win-the-2028-repu.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Florida governor Ron DeSantis wins the Republican presidential nomination for 2028. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, a running gauge of his standing against the party's other contenders.

poly-us-iran-ceasefire-continues-through.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the ceasefire between the United States and Iran survives until the US midterm elections. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, talks and Gulf shipping.
poly-us-iran-ceasefire-continues-through.recent: Araghchi, in Baghdad, set Iran's terms: it would reopen Hormuz within six days and resume talks with the US on the seventh if Washington accepts its conditions. The offer came in a week when Iran's army said it fired on 3 ships and the IRGC said a supertanker struck a mine.

poly-will-aleksandar-vucic-united-serbia.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Serbian Progressive Party, the party Aleksandar Vučić built, wins the most seats in Serbia's 2026 parliamentary election. SNS has won the most seats in every vote since 2012.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if U.S. forces invade Iran before 2027. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it separates bets on a ground war from bets on air and naval strikes.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: The war with the US has been fought from the air and the sea: Trump threatened Iran's buried nuclear sites such as Fordow with a 9,800kg bomb, the US pulled its bombers out of RAF Fairford, and ships sank or struck mines off Hormuz. In Baghdad, Araghchi offered to reopen the strait within six days and resume talks with the US on the seventh.

poly-will-delcy-rodrguez-be-the-leader-o.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Delcy Rodríguez is leading Venezuela when 2026 ends. Long Nicolás Maduro's vice president, she is the figure traders bet on to hold or lose power through the country's transition.

poly-will-anthropic-ipo-by-november-30-2.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the San Francisco developer of the Claude AI models, lists its shares publicly by November 30, 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

stocks:AVGO.standing: A US chipmaker that designs the custom AI accelerators and networking silicon the largest cloud companies build their data centres on. It also owns VMware, whose software runs much of the world's corporate server estate.
stocks:AVGO.recent: Broadcom joined Verizon and 7 other issuers in refusing to have its stock tokenized under the SEC's temporary framework, which lets crypto venues such as OKX list tokens of public companies' shares. A survey found licensing costs driving 90 percent of VMware users to explore options. Neither accounts for the share's fall.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Saudi Arabia, the Gulf kingdom that is the world's largest oil exporter and the guardian of Mecca and Medina. It counts how many people looked the country up, not what happened there.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Houthi missiles hit Riyadh airport twice, killing 13 and wounding over 300, and Lufthansa, Air India and Qatar Airways halted flights to Riyadh and Dammam. The war is pulling in allies: Pakistan's army confirmed troops already in Saudi Arabia, and Egypt's council approved sending its own.

stocks:NDAQ.standing: Runs the Nasdaq Stock Market and exchanges in the Nordics and Baltics, and earns more from market data, index licensing and anti-fraud software than from trades. Funds that track the Nasdaq-100 pay it a licence fee.
stocks:NDAQ.recent: Nasdaq joined Broadcom and Verizon in objecting to the SEC's temporary framework, which lets crypto venues such as OKX list tokens of a company's shares without that company's consent. The objection came after the last close shown and does not account for the share price.

stocks:VZ.standing: One of the three national US mobile carriers alongside AT&T and T-Mobile, also selling home broadband and fibre. It carries heavy debt from spectrum purchases, and its large dividend makes it an income stock for many holders.
stocks:VZ.recent: Shares fell hardest when SpaceX struck a nationwide low-band spectrum deal for Starlink Mobile, bringing a satellite rival onto the airwaves carriers sell, and AT&T dropped alongside it. Separately, Verizon joined Broadcom and Nasdaq in objecting to the SEC framework that lets crypto venues such as OKX list tokens of its stock without its consent.

poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the US, Russian and Chinese leaders meet together in person before 2027. A three-way meeting would put Beijing at the table on matters Washington and Moscow usually settle between themselves.
poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.recent: Trump waived the 500% tariffs on Russian energy before they began, and Putin then proposed a three-way summit next month with Trump and Xi to settle the Ukraine war on terms that favour Moscow, the Wall Street Journal reports. The format would seat Beijing at the table and leave Kyiv and Europe outside it.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats win a majority in the US House of Representatives at the 2026 midterms. The House controls federal spending and can open investigations into the White House.

poly-will-anthropic-announce-bankruptcy-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the AI lab that makes Claude, goes bankrupt before the end of 2027. It is a wager on whether the cost of training frontier models outruns the capital raised to pay for it.

poly-trump-out-as-president-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Donald Trump stops being president before 2027, whether by resignation, removal or death. It prices what traders will pay against him serving out a term that runs to January 2029.
poly-trump-out-as-president-before-2027.recent: The fortnight's news about the White House: Katie Zacharia ousted as press secretary after five days, Trump promising jail for California officials who count flagged ballots, his cheap-energy pledge undone by Brent. None of it touched any route out of office, and none of it accounts for the price.

poly-perim-island-no-longer-under-houthi.standing: A bet on whether Perim, a small island in the Bab al-Mandeb strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa, is taken from the Houthis by Dec 31. Whoever holds it overlooks the channel that Red Sea shipping to Suez must pass.
poly-perim-island-no-longer-under-houthi.recent: Yemen's government said its forces had taken Dhubab and cut the Mocha road on the push toward Bab al-Mandeb, claims the other side disputed. No further advance along the coast has been reported since. The war's news moved to Houthi missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh's airport, Yanbu and Aramco.

poly-will-jon-ossoff-win-the-2028-democr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Jon Ossoff, the Democratic senator from Georgia, becomes his party's 2028 presidential nominee. The price is what traders pay, in cents per dollar of payout.

poly-will-there-be-no-hormuz-agreement.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if no deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is reached by its deadline. The strait carries much of the world's seaborne oil and Gulf gas, so its closure reaches fuel and fertilizer prices worldwide.
poly-will-there-be-no-hormuz-agreement.recent: A weekly record of 12 ships attacked near Hormuz came with an IRGC claim that a 2-million-barrel supertanker hit a mine. Then Araghchi, in Baghdad, offered to reopen the strait within six days, with talks with Washington resuming on the seventh if it accepts Iran's conditions, while Gulf states urged Lavrov to press Tehran.

stocks:SPLS.standing: A PIMCO exchange-traded fund that pairs exposure to US stocks with an actively managed bond portfolio, so its price reflects both the American equity market and the bond returns its managers add on top.

poly-no-hormuz-agreement-by-nov-2.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether no agreement is reached to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the channel carrying much of the world's seaborne oil and Gulf exports. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.
poly-no-hormuz-agreement-by-nov-2.recent: Araghchi, in Baghdad, offered to reopen Hormuz within six days and resume talks with the US on the seventh if Washington accepts Iran's terms, while Gulf states sent Lavrov to Tehran to press Iran on shipping. That came after a record week of 12 ships attacked near Hormuz and a supertanker the IRGC said struck a mine.

stocks:DTE.DE.standing: Germany's former state phone monopoly, based in Bonn, and Europe's largest telecom operator by revenue. Most of its earnings come from its controlling stake in T-Mobile US, so the dollar and American wireless competition move it.

stocks:ORA.PA.standing: France's largest telecoms operator, formerly the state monopoly France Télécom, selling mobile and broadband across Europe and Africa. The French state remains its largest shareholder.

stocks:TEF.MC.standing: Spain's former state telephone monopoly, which runs Movistar at home, O2 in Germany and Vivo in Brazil. Its heavy debt and Latin American earnings tie the share to interest rates and the Brazilian real.

stocks:VOD.standing: Vodafone, one of Europe's largest mobile operators, based in England with networks across Europe and, through Vodacom, Africa. This is its US-listed share, priced in dollars, so sterling moves reach it too.

stocks:VSAT.standing: A Carlsbad, California satellite operator that bought Inmarsat in 2023. It sells broadband to airlines, ships and the US military from geostationary orbit, and competes with low-orbit fleets such as Starlink.

stocks:ETL.PA.standing: A Paris-listed satellite operator that runs geostationary broadcast satellites and the OneWeb low-orbit broadband constellation, Europe's main commercial alternative to Starlink.

stocks:VOW3.DE.standing: Europe's largest carmaker, based in Wolfsburg and owner of Audi, Porsche, Skoda and SEAT. Its shares price whether a combustion-era giant can sell electric cars in China and keep its German plants full.
stocks:VOW3.DE.recent: The only company news in the input landed after this window closed: Volkswagen plans to give 660,000 workers no raises until 2030, a pay freeze across its global workforce. Nothing in the input accounts for the slide before it.

poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by November 2. Its price is what traders will stake on a deal that would reopen the Gulf's main oil export route.
poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.recent: Traders pulled back as attacks on ships near Hormuz hit a weekly record of 12 and the IRGC said a supertanker struck a mine. They returned once Araghchi, in Baghdad, offered to reopen the strait within 6 days, with talks resuming the next day if Washington accepts, and Gulf states sent Lavrov to Tehran to press Iran on shipping.

poly-will-yashar-win-the-most-seats-in-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Yashar, the party Gadi Eisenkot founded, takes the most Knesset seats in Israel's 2026 election. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, not a poll.
poly-will-yashar-win-the-most-seats-in-t.recent: The fortnight's reporting from Israel carried Ronen Bar's defamation suit against Netanyahu over October 7 and settler attacks in the West Bank, but nothing about Yashar or its standing that accounts for the price.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at its December 2026 meeting. Its price is what traders will pay for a hold rather than a hike or a cut.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Most Federal Reserve officials now expect another rate hike by year-end, with US inflation above the Fed's target for 5.5 years. In Bangkok, Warsh called AI a shock to the economy and withheld guidance on the next move, while the IMF praised his focus on price stability.

poly-putin-out-as-president-of-russia-by.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Vladimir Putin stops being Russia's president before June 2027, for any reason. Constitutional changes in 2020 let him run again, and no term limit forces him out before 2036.
poly-putin-out-as-president-of-russia-by.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news bore on Putin's hold on office. It showed Moscow pressing its hand instead: Putin proposed a summit with Trump and Xi that would leave Kyiv outside the room, and Trump put on hold new Russia sanctions he had signed into law.

wiki-data-center.standing: A building packed with the servers, storage and network links that run cloud services, websites and AI models. It draws large, constant amounts of power and cooling water, so where one can be built depends on the local grid.
wiki-data-center.recent: Ukrainian drones have hit 3 of Yandex's 6 Russian data centers, and another struck Sberbank's in Balakovo, turning server halls into targets in the war. Iran then warned that Gulf cables and data centres could be attacked, while in Belém, Elea's AI data center went ahead without an environmental licence.

poly-ex-cuba-leader-raul-castro-in-us-cu.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Raúl Castro, Fidel's brother, Cuba's president from 2008 to 2018 and party chief until 2021, is in US custody by year's end. Traders bet on Washington getting him before an American court.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Marco Rubio becomes the Republican Party's 2028 presidential nominee. Its price is what traders will pay on him winning the party's first open race after Trump.

poly-will-raphal-glucksmann-win-the-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Raphaël Glucksmann, the centre-left MEP who leads Place Publique, wins France's 2027 presidential election. Its price is the bet on a fractured left uniting behind him.

poly-will-likud-win-30-34-seats-in-the-2.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Likud, Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing party, wins between 30 and 34 of the Knesset's 120 seats in Israel's 2026 election. Its price is what traders will pay for that band.
poly-will-likud-win-30-34-seats-in-the-2.recent: Netanyahu spent the fortnight answering ex-Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar's 3 million shekel defamation suit over October 7, and alleging a smear after settlers beat a French mayor in Taybeh. Neither story carries a poll or a seat count, and nothing in them accounts for the bets on Likud.
